summary: Shlomo Pines worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. Between 1926 and 1934, he studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Berlin. He taught at the University of Paris and Institut d'histoire des sciences (1937–1939) and was a philosophy professor at Hebrew University (1952–1990).

Specializing in philosophy and history/archaeology, Shmuel Sambursky studied at the University of Königsberg (~1920–1923) and the University of Berlin (~1923–1924). He held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from circa 1928 to 1970.
Shobha Rani Dash works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was an open-recruitment researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010 and is attested as a lecturer at Otani University in 2012.
Shodo Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami and Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).
Buddhist studies scholar Shodo Harada studied under Mumon Yamada (1962–1982) and at Shofukuji (~1968–1982). He became abbot at Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Shogo Watanabe studied at Toyo University. He later joined Toyo University, where his post is attested in 1991 and he served as a professor around 2002.

Buddhist studies specialist Shohaku Okumura studied at Komazawa University (~1968–1972) and under Kosho Uchiyama (1970–1975). He held posts at Pioneer Valley Zendo, Kyoto Soto Zen Center, Minnesota Zen Meditation Center, and the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center.

Shoji Mori studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Toyo University (~1962–1971) under Giyu Nishi. He was a researcher at Okura Institute for the Study of Spiritual Culture (~1971–1979) before serving as assistant professor (~1979–1985) and professor (~1985–2009) at Toyo University.
Shoju Inaba specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor at Otani University (attested 1962) and as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.
Shojun Bando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Ueno Gakuen University and Otani University.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Shokin Furuta studied at Matsue High School, Shimane University, University of Tokyo (~1933–1936), and Tokyo University of Education (-1961), learning from Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He held professorships at Hokkaido (~1958–1974) and Nihon (~1975–1981) universities.
Specializing in Sinology and Buddhist studies, Shoko Kanaoka held an academic career at Toyo University, where he is attested as a professor in 1987 and attested again in 2000.

Shoko Miyabayashi, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, studied at Taisho University (1948–~1955). He spent his academic career at Taisho University, serving as lecturer (1960), assistant professor (1962), and Dean of Buddhist Studies (1978–2002).

Shoko Takeuchi specialized in Buddhist studies, graduating from Ryukoku University. He maintained a long affiliation with Ryukoku University, where he served as professor emeritus (attested 1987–1995) and is attested again in 2009.

Shoko Watanabe studied Buddhist studies and Indology at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University under Ernst Leumann and Naoshiro Tsuji. His posts included Taisho University (1935–1943), Kyushu University (1948–1953), and Toyo University (1956–1969).

Shoku Bando studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg (1984–1986). In 1987, he held appointments at the Abhidharma Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Shoren Ihara was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held positions at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1965 as assistant professor, and 1977) and the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

Shoryu Katsura studied at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, his main appointments included Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and director at Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara studied Buddhist studies at Otani University and Hōryū-ji under Join Saeki and Susumu Yamaguchi. He held teaching posts at Otani Senshu Gakuin, Shinshu College, Doho University, Otani University Junior College, and Otani University.

Shoshin Ichishima was a Buddhist studies scholar. He held positions at Taisho University, where he was Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2014), and served as a visiting lecturer at the University of Hawaiʻi.
